components.subtitle: A 20-minute one-pan fried rice made with aged kimchi and its juice.

components.label: Cook time
components.caption: Fry rice, then crisp the bottom

components.title: Ingredients
components.description: Sour, aged kimchi works best — fresh kimchi tastes flat here.

components.title: Steps
components.description: Do not stir until the rice has crisped — that is the whole trick.

items.title: Prep the kimchi
items.description: Squeeze the kimchi from the jar and chop it into 2 cm pieces. Measure 2 tbsp of the juice.

items.title: Fry the aromatics
items.description: Heat the neutral oil over medium-high. Add the kimchi and garlic, stir-fry until the edges caramelize and smell toasty.

items.title: Add the rice
items.description: Add cold day-old rice and break it apart with the spatula. Add kimchi juice, soy sauce, sugar and gochugaru; toss until every grain is red.

items.title: Crisp the bottom
items.description: Stop stirring. Press the rice flat, drizzle the sesame oil around the edge, and let it sizzle undisturbed until the bottom crackles.

items.title: Egg and finish
items.description: Push the rice to one side, crack in the eggs and fry until the edges are lacy. Fold over the rice, scatter green onion and sesame seeds.

items.title: Serve
items.description: Split into two bowls. A drizzle of sesame oil and a sheet of nori on top, if you like.

components.title: Two things that decide the dish
components.text: Use **cold, day-old rice** — fresh rice steams and turns gummy. And **do not stir** during the last 5 minutes; the crackling crust is the best part.
Quantities are for 2 servings. Illustrative recipe card.
